extraction.extract_command: LEAN_INVENTORY_OUT=... LEAN_INVENTORY_MODULES=... LEAN_INVENTORY_SHARD=k/n bash scripts/coord-tools/gate.sh per-file scripts/lean-inventory/Extract.lean

limitations: The kernel theorem Solidity.LeanInventory.inventory_sound certifies only the abstract certificate reasoning of Solidity.Goals.Inventory; it does not certify this Python extraction or its completeness, any elapsed time, Git recovery, or deletion safety.
Adequate (every actual use recorded or covered by a listed gap) is an external input obligation of the real census and is not established by any proof or by this tool.

Edges are kernel-term constants of elaborated declarations (types, values, inductive, constructor and recursor links), implemented_by targets, and project names quoted in metaprogram values; elaborator-time uses (tactics, macros, elaborators, instance and simp-set lookups by commands that leave no constant) are not edges and are represented by the implicit-use gaps.
Uses by anonymous commands (example, #guard, #eval, ...) are the explicit identifier references Lean records in .ilean files; their implicit uses are covered by the implicit-use gaps, not observed.

Lean files outside the built libraries (tests/, Bridge/, scripts/, docs/, vscode/, web/) and Lean text generated by runner scripts are not elaborated; their possible uses are gaps bounded by the exact import closure of their headers or of the import lines found in runner text (a dynamic import name is bounded by its static prefix). Runner text that builds an import from data without a static prefix is not detected.
Grouping, command classification, attribute detection and runner import detection are lexical; they only bound gaps or propose candidates and never establish a use or absence.
Check times come from one recorded Lake build of this revision on a 4-core VM with parallel jobs; modules fetched from the Lake artifact cache have no measured time.
unresolved is the conservative verdict: it is precise only as far as the listed gaps; certified orphan families are deletion candidates only, not deletion evidence.

scope.grouping_rule: A module D/XControls.lean or D/XPins.lean, and D/X.lean when either exists, form the family triple:D/X with roles controls, pins and member; D/Controls.lean and D/Pins.lean are the controls/pins of the directory family dir:D/; every other in-scope module belongs to dir:D/ of its own directory (not recursive).
scope.identity: a declaration is a kernel constant with a declaration range; auxiliary constants fold into their nearest ranged name prefix (uses folded alike); module@line is an anonymous check inside the areas (a Controls/Pins one is a demand seed)

line_basis: physical lines of the Git blob at the revision (newline-terminated lines plus a final unterminated one)

recovery.command: git show 3046d5aa87ddb37cd35d0467a8dfa421749aa86e:PATH  (PATH: any member path below)

provenance.source: Lake "Built" job times of one incremental build of the library roots (lake lean through gate.sh per-file), possibly interrupted and resumed over several runs, some at an ancestor revision; the logs are concatenated in run order and a later time overrides. Lake rebuilds a module whose source or imports changed, so each measured time is of the last elaboration of that module, whose inputs match this revision
provenance.context: Lake artifact cache seeded by scripts/ci/fetch-lake-cache.sh; 4-core VM, parallel Lake jobs; Lean sources identical to the analyzed revision (lean_tree_id 18973365798f9574)

timing.unavailable_reason: fetched from the Lake artifact cache in the recorded build (no elaboration measured) or not built there
timing.member_field: members rows: [path, role, lines, declarations, anonymous checks, check ms or null when unavailable]

blanket.reason: whole-library axiom audit (header lines 1-20): a scan of every constant, not a use of any one

rules: goal:D: a registered @[goal] whose expected proof exists; root = that proof.
test:P: a module built only by a test library (SolidityExamples, SoliditySlowExamples, SolkeyTestSuite, SolidityCorpus); roots = its theorems and the references of its anonymous commands.
check:P: anonymous commands of a library module outside the areas; roots = their references.
exe:E: a lean_exe main; roots = project constants its root module reaches.

An anonymous check inside an area is a declaration of its module (module@line), not a consumer: in Controls/Pins it is a demand seed; in a member module it is deleted with its family and demands nothing.

gaps.reason: metaprogram (type mentions the Lean namespace): run by the elaborator while checking other declarations, which leaves no kernel-term constant
metaprogram possibly run by an anonymous command (no recorded constant)
instance, simp lemma or attribute-registered declaration: an anonymous check inside the areas may use it implicitly (instance or simp-set lookup), which its .ilean references do not record
instance, simp lemma or attribute-registered declaration possibly used implicitly by an anonymous command outside the areas
Lean text written by a runner script whose import lines reach this module
referenced from a command outside every declaration that the lexical command classifier cannot place (consumer or not)
Lean file outside the built libraries (not elaborated here) whose header import closure reaches this module

witness.empty: no declarations in any member module
no declarations in any member module
